sources.freshness_role: Dated, current firm update names 3 November 2026 and directs readers to check open positions, position size and risk per trade; it also warns that order fills may differ in fast markets. It is not used to assert that any market will move, that a fill will differ, or that any account should trade.
Independent government page confirms that the next U.S. midterm elections are in November 2026; it verifies event context only and is not a market, broker, prop-firm or trading source.

Public updated calendar provides discovery context that prop-trader audiences are following the current high-impact week. It is not used to verify FTMO scope, event facts, market conditions or any calculation output.

decision.reopen_trigger: No refresh after the result-count window. Reopen only if FTMO publishes a new dated, applicable update or a distinct verified rule/calculation query; otherwise retire the event framing.
decision.rationale: This is not election commentary: a dated FTMO notice creates a short, firm-specific and non-directional reader task—add reader-entered planned stop losses across open positions before reacting to a fast market. The natural bridge is PipGauge Portfolio Heat plus Pip Value/Position Size, with transparent hypothetical inputs and no prediction, execution assertion or trade instruction. No materially similar FTMO election package exists in the ledger.

sources.freshness_role: Official announcement records a 25bp increase to a 4.85% cash-rate target and a 6-3 vote.
Independent English coverage confirms the result and vote context. It is not used to forecast AUD/USD, policy, volatility or an execution outcome.
Public result-day page demonstrates current attention, but retained comments are direction/volatility led and are not evidence of a calculator request or policy fact.

decision.reopen_trigger: Require an attributable public RBA-result-specific fixed-risk, pip-value, margin, cost, quantity or portfolio-heat question and at least one additional refresh signal; then refresh the existing RBA article rather than make a parallel AUD/USD sizing post.
decision.rationale: The new 4.85% result meets factual freshness, but current public attention remains about AUD direction and rate-path interpretation. Reusing another generic 20/40/80-pip grid would invent a calculator journey.
